anat-gi-organs.intro: Walk down the GI tract the way you'll treat it: esophagus → GEJ and stomach → pancreas → liver → rectum → anal canal. For each organ, know its regions and the landmarks that change staging and surgery. Explore each view, then switch to Quiz mode.

plates.title: Esophagus: Segments by Distance
plates.caption: The esophagus from the cricopharyngeus to the stomach. The pale bands mark the upper, middle, and lower thirds. Cancer Research UK diagram (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed.

hotspots.label: Cricopharyngeus (~15 cm)
hotspots.blurb: Upper esophageal sphincter: the start of the esophagus. Cervical esophagus runs from here to the thoracic inlet (~20 cm). Cervical tumors are treated like head and neck (definitive chemoRT).

hotspots.label: Upper Thoracic (20–25 cm)
hotspots.blurb: Thoracic inlet to the azygos vein. Behind the trachea. Mostly squamous cell.

hotspots.label: Carina Level (~25 cm)
hotspots.blurb: Tumors here can invade the airway (fistula risk); bronchoscopy for upper/mid tumors.

hotspots.label: Middle Thoracic (25–30 cm)
hotspots.blurb: Behind the left atrium. SCC more common.

hotspots.label: Lower Thoracic (30–40 cm)
hotspots.blurb: Where adenocarcinoma (Barrett's) arises.

hotspots.label: Diaphragmatic Hiatus
hotspots.blurb: Where the esophagus passes into the abdomen.

hotspots.label: Gastroesophageal Junction (~40 cm)
hotspots.blurb: Siewert I (1–5 cm above), II (at the junction), III (2–5 cm below). I and II are treated like esophageal cancer.

plates.title: Stomach & GEJ Regions
plates.caption: The stomach and first part of the duodenum, front view. Cancer Research UK diagram (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed.

hotspots.label: Cardia
hotspots.blurb: Just below the GEJ. Tumors near here behave like GEJ cancers.

hotspots.label: Fundus
hotspots.blurb: Top of the stomach under the left diaphragm.

hotspots.label: Body
hotspots.blurb: Largest part.

hotspots.label: Antrum
hotspots.blurb: Lower stomach. Distal gastric cancers are the classic intestinal-type, H. pylori-related tumors.

hotspots.label: Pylorus
hotspots.blurb: Outlet into the duodenum; tumors here cause gastric outlet obstruction.

hotspots.label: Lesser Curvature
hotspots.blurb: Left gastric nodes run along it.

hotspots.label: Greater Curvature
hotspots.blurb: Gastroepiploic nodes; attaches to the omentum.

plates.title: Pancreas & Its Vessels (Posterior View)
plates.caption: The pancreas and duodenum seen from BEHIND, so the head sits on the right of the picture and the tail on the left. Gray H, Anatomy of the Human Body (1918), Fig. 1099 (Wikimedia Commons), public domain.

hotspots.label: Pancreatic Head
hotspots.blurb: ~70% of pancreatic cancers. Blocks the bile duct early: painless jaundice (and the 'double duct' sign).

hotspots.label: Uncinate Process
hotspots.blurb: Hooks behind the SMV; tumors here often contact the SMA/SMV.

hotspots.label: Neck
hotspots.blurb: Sits directly over the SMV/portal vein confluence.

hotspots.label: Body
hotspots.blurb: Body/tail tumors present later (pain, weight loss) and are often unresectable.

hotspots.label: Tail
hotspots.blurb: Near the splenic hilum.

hotspots.label: Superior Mesenteric Artery (SMA)
hotspots.blurb: Encasement >180° = locally advanced.

hotspots.label: SMV / Portal Vein
hotspots.blurb: Venous involvement can be reconstructed at surgery (borderline).

hotspots.label: Celiac Axis
hotspots.blurb: Encasement = locally advanced; celiac plexus pain from tumor invasion.

hotspots.label: Common Bile Duct
hotspots.blurb: Runs through the head; stented for jaundice.

hotspots.label: Duodenum (C-loop)
hotspots.blurb: Wraps the head. Key SBRT OAR (bleeding/ulcer).

plates.title: Liver: Lobes & Vessels
plates.caption: The liver's right and left lobes with the portal vein (dark blue), hepatic artery (red), hepatic veins (light blue), and bile ducts (green). The caudate lobe (segment I) is not visible from this angle; see the Couinaud model below. Cancer Research UK diagram (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed.

hotspots.label: Right Lobe (Segments V–VIII)
hotspots.blurb: The larger lobe; resections are planned by segment.

hotspots.label: Left Lobe (Segments II–IV)
hotspots.blurb: Segment IV is the medial left lobe.

hotspots.label: Portal Vein
hotspots.blurb: Tumor thrombus in the portal vein is common in HCC and changes treatment (SBRT can treat it).

hotspots.label: Hepatic Veins / IVC
hotspots.blurb: Divide the liver into sectors; drain to the IVC.

hotspots.label: Gallbladder
hotspots.blurb: Marks the division between right and left lobes (Cantlie's line with the IVC).

hotspots.label: Liver Dome
hotspots.blurb: Right under the diaphragm: moves a lot with breathing (motion management for SBRT).

hotspots.label: Hepatic Artery
hotspots.blurb: Runs beside the portal vein. HCC gets most of its blood supply from the hepatic artery, which is why it lights up in the arterial phase and why TACE works.

hotspots.label: Common Bile Duct
hotspots.blurb: Drains bile from the liver and gallbladder down to the duodenum. Central liver tumors near the hilum risk biliary stricture after SBRT.

plates.title: Rectum & Anal Canal
plates.caption: Left: sagittal drawing of the rectum with the mesorectal fascia (thick line), peritoneum (double line), and the high/mid/low levels. Right: coronal drawing of the anal canal. Bogveradze N et al., Insights Imaging 2023 (PMC9849549), Figs. 8 and 4, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Upper Rectum (10–15 cm)
hotspots.blurb: Above the peritoneal reflection anteriorly; behaves more like sigmoid colon (RT less often needed).

hotspots.label: Anterior Peritoneal Reflection
hotspots.blurb: Tumor above it that breaches the peritoneum = T4a.

hotspots.label: Mid Rectum (5–10 cm)
hotspots.blurb: Surrounded by mesorectal fat.

hotspots.label: Low Rectum (0–5 cm)
hotspots.blurb: Thin mesorectum: higher risk of positive margins and APR.

hotspots.label: Mesorectum
hotspots.blurb: Fat, vessels, and nodes around the rectum: removed en bloc in a TME.

hotspots.label: Mesorectal Fascia (MRF)
hotspots.blurb: The surgical margin. Tumor ≤1 mm from it = threatened CRM.

hotspots.label: Anorectal Ring / Puborectalis
hotspots.blurb: Top of the anal canal; the levators are here.

hotspots.label: Dentate Line
hotspots.blurb: Above: mesorectal/internal iliac drainage. Below: inguinal drainage.

hotspots.label: Internal & External Sphincters
hotspots.blurb: Invasion doesn't make anal cancer T4; it affects whether a rectal tumor can be sphincter-sparing.

hotspots.label: Anal Verge
hotspots.blurb: The zero point for measuring rectal tumor height.

gallery.title: Endoscopy: Barrett's
gallery.caption: Salmon-colored columnar mucosa extending above the EGJ (arrows mark the top of the gastric folds). Japan Esophageal Society, Esophagus 2017 (PMC5222925), Fig. 2-1d, CC BY 4.0.

gallery.title: Couinaud segments
gallery.caption: The liver from below with its functional segments numbered; segment 1 (caudate) sits next to the IVC. BodyParts3D/DBCLS (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY-SA 2.1 JP.

anat-gi-nodes.intro: Each GI organ drains along its blood supply. Learn the nodal basins for the three sites you'll treat most: the esophagus/stomach, the pancreas, and the rectum/anus.

plates.title: Esophagus & Stomach Nodes
plates.caption: Japanese Esophageal Society node stations along the esophagus and stomach (numbers are the JES/JGCA station names; colors show nodal grouping for GEJ cancers in the source, legend removed). Liang R et al., Front Oncol 2022 (PMC9743047), Fig. 1A, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Supraclavicular Nodes (104)
hotspots.blurb: Distant (M1) for esophageal cancer; included electively for some cervical/upper tumors.

hotspots.label: Paratracheal Nodes (106rec)
hotspots.blurb: Upper thoracic drainage.

hotspots.label: Subcarinal Nodes (107)
hotspots.blurb: Mid esophagus.

hotspots.label: Paraesophageal Nodes (108 / 110)
hotspots.blurb: Along the whole esophagus; skip spread is common.

hotspots.label: Left Gastric Nodes (7)
hotspots.blurb: Along the lesser curvature; first echelon for distal esophagus/GEJ.

hotspots.label: Celiac Nodes (9)
hotspots.blurb: Regional for distal esophagus and stomach; included in GEJ fields.

hotspots.label: Perigastric Nodes (1–6)
hotspots.blurb: Along both curvatures.

plates.title: Pancreas Nodes
plates.caption: Schematic of the pancreatic node groups around the celiac axis, SMA, and splenic artery. Cho HS, Ahn JH, J Korean Soc Radiol 2022 (PMC9748447), Fig. 22A, CC BY-NC 4.0.

hotspots.label: Peripancreatic (Pancreaticoduodenal) Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Regional (N1 = 1–3 nodes, N2 = ≥4).

hotspots.label: Hepatic Artery Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Regional.

hotspots.label: Celiac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Regional for the pancreas.

hotspots.label: SMA Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Regional; around the SMA root.

hotspots.label: Para-aortic Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Distant (M1).

hotspots.label: Splenic Hilar Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Body/tail tumors.

plates.title: Rectal & Anal Nodes
plates.caption: Rectal cancer node stations drawn on a 3D reconstruction (a) and axial T2 MRI at three levels (b to d): mesorectal (orange), obturator (green), internal iliac (yellow), external iliac (blue). Inguinal nodes sit below this field. Bogveradze N et al., Insights Imaging 2023 (PMC9849549), Fig. 12, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Mesorectal Nodes (Mes)
hotspots.blurb: First echelon for the rectum; removed with TME.

hotspots.label: Superior Rectal / IMA Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Along the superior rectal and inferior mesenteric vessels (upper rectum).

hotspots.label: Internal Iliac Nodes (II)
hotspots.blurb: Lateral drainage of the mid/low rectum; regional.

hotspots.label: Obturator Nodes (O)
hotspots.blurb: Lateral; regional for rectum (lateral node group).

hotspots.label: Presacral Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Regional; included in rectal fields.

hotspots.label: External Iliac Nodes (EI)
hotspots.blurb: Regional for anal cancer; distant for rectal cancer unless an anterior organ is invaded.
